academic_translation:
Unruly sentient beings are like space;
They can never be fully overcome.
If this single mind of anger is overcome,
It is as if all those enemies were overcome.
translation: Wild living beings are as endless as space. They can never be fully defeated. But if this single mind of anger is defeated, it is like defeating all those enemies at once.

academic_translation:
To cover this surface of the earth with leather,
How could there be enough leather?
With just the leather for the soles of one's shoes,
It is as if the entire surface of the earth were covered.
translation: How could there ever be enough leather to cover the whole earth? But with just enough leather for the soles of your shoes, it is as if the whole earth is covered.
In the same way, I cannot stop every outside thing. I will just stop this mind of mine. What need is there to stop anything else?

academic_translation:
Whatever the result of generating a single clear mind,
Such as Brahmā and so forth,
The result, even when accompanied by body and speech,
Because of weak conduct, is not like that.
translation: Having just one clear mind brings a great result. It can make you like Brahma. But if your actions are weak, just using your body and words will not bring a result like that.

academic_translation:
All recitations and austerities,
Even if practiced for a long time,
If performed with a mind distracted elsewhere,
Are said by the Knower of Reality to be meaningless.

locked_terms.use: Knower of the way things really are

translation: You might do recitation and hard practice for a long time. But if you do them with a wandering mind, they are meaningless. The Knower of the way things really are said this.

academic_translation:
Whoever does not know the supreme principal of the Dharma,
This secret of the mind,
Even though they wish to attain happiness and overcome suffering,
They will wander meaninglessly and in vain.
translation: Some people do not know the most important part of the teachings. They do not know this secret of the mind. They want to find happiness and end suffering. But they will just wander around for no reason.

academic_translation:
Therefore, this mind of mine
I shall hold well and properly guard.
Except for the ascetic discipline of guarding the mind,
What is the use of many ascetic disciplines?
translation: Because of this, I will carefully hold and protect this mind of mine. What is the point of doing many kinds of strict practice? The only one I need is the strict practice of guarding the mind.

academic_translation:
When dwelling in the midst of an unruly crowd,
Just as one carefully protects a wound,
So too, when dwelling among bad people,
One should always guard this wound of the mind.
translation: If you are in a wild crowd, you carefully protect a bodily wound. In the same way, when you are around bad people, you must always protect this wound of the mind.

academic_translation:
If even one afraid of the minor suffering of a wound
Carefully protects a wound,
Why do those who fear the Crushing Hell and Destroying hell
Not guard the wound of the mind?
translation: A person carefully protects a scratch because they fear the small suffering of a wound. So why do people who fear the Crushing Hell and Destroying hell not guard the wound of the mind?

academic_translation:
If one abides in such conduct,
Whether dwelling among wicked people
Or even dwelling among women,
The steadfast practitioner of restraint will not decline.
translation: If a person acts like this, they will stay strong. Whether living among bad people or among women, a steady person of self-restraint will not fail.

academic_translation:
Better that my gain and honor
And my body and livelihood perish,
And better that other virtues decline,
But I must never let my mind decline.
translation: It is better to lose my gain and honor. It is better to lose my body and my life. It is even better to lose other good deeds. But I must never let my mind fail.

academic_translation:
To those who wish to guard the mind,
"Both mindfulness and introspection,
Guard them with all your effort!"—saying this,
I thus join my palms together.
translation: To those who want to guard the mind, I put my hands together and ask this. Guard both keeping in mind and watchfulness with all your effort!

academic_translation:
People who are disturbed by illness
Are powerless in all activities;
Likewise, the mind disturbed by delusion
Is powerless in all activities.
translation: People who are troubled by illness have no power to do anything. In the same way, a mind troubled by confusion has no power to do anything.

academic_translation:
For one who has a mind lacking introspection,
Even what is heard, pondered, and meditated upon,
Like water in a leaking vase,
Does not remain in mindfulness.
translation: If someone has a mind without watchfulness, what they hear, think about, and practice will leak out. Like water in a cracked pot, it does not stay in keeping in mind.

academic_translation:
Even many who possess learning and faith,
And who are dedicated to diligence,
By incurring the fault of lacking introspection,
Will become tainted by the stain of downfalls.
translation: Many people have learning and faith. Many people work hard with great effort. But if they make the mistake of lacking watchfulness, they will be stained by a fall.

academic_translation:
Because the thieves of a lack of introspection
Follow upon the decline of mindfulness,
Even when merits have been accumulated,
One goes to the lower realms, as if robbed by thieves.
translation: When keeping in mind fades away, the thieves of lost watchfulness sneak in. Even if I have gathered a store of goodness, they rob me. Then I go down to an unhappy realm.

academic_translation:
This band of affliction thieves
Searches for an opportunity;
Having found an opportunity, they steal virtue,
And destroy even the life of a happy realm.
translation: This gang of thieves, made of troubling emotions, looks for a chance to strike. When they find it, they steal every good deed. They even destroy life in a happy realm.

academic_translation:
Therefore, one should never let mindfulness go
From the gateway of the mind.
Even if it departs, recalling the harms of the lower realms,
One should closely establish it.
translation: So, I must never let keeping in mind wander away from the door of the mind. If it does leave, I should remember the pain of the unhappy realms and bring it right back.

academic_translation:
From associating with a teacher,
And the instruction of a preceptor,
For fortunate ones who act with respect out of fear,
Mindfulness is easily generated.
translation: For lucky people who act with careful respect, keeping in mind grows easily. This happens by spending time with a teacher and listening to the teacher who ordained me.

academic_translation:
The Buddhas and bodhisattvas
Possess unobstructed vision everywhere.
"In the presence of them all,
I always dwell."
translation: The Buddhas and awakening heroes can see everywhere without anything blocking their view. I should think, "I am always standing right in front of them all."

academic_translation:
Having thought in this way, with shame,
Respect, and fear, one should thus take it on and remain so.
Therefore, the recollection of the Buddha
Will also arise in one again and again.
translation: Thinking this way, I should act with shame, respect, and fear. By doing this, keeping the Buddha in mind will happen to me again and again.

academic_translation:
When mindfulness at the gateway of the mind
Remains for the sake of guarding,
At that time introspection will come,
And even that which has gone will return.
translation: When keeping in mind stays at the door of the mind to guard it, watchfulness will come. Even what was lost will come back.

academic_translation:
First, having recognized a mind such as this
To be faulty,
At that time I, like a log of wood,
Should remain steadfast.
translation: First, when I see that a mind like this has faults, I should stay firm like a log of wood.

academic_translation:
Looking around distractedly without purpose
I should never do;
With a resolute mind, I should always
Look with eyes cast down.
translation: I should never look around for no reason. With a firm mind, I should always look down.

academic_translation:
For the sake of resting the gaze,
Occasionally I should look in the directions;
If someone appears in my field of vision,
I should look at them and say, "Welcome."
translation: To rest my eyes, I should sometimes look around. If I see someone, I should look at them and say, "Welcome."

academic_translation:
To check for dangers on the path and so forth,
I should look repeatedly in the four directions;
Having rested, turning to look back,
I should look toward the area behind.
translation: To check for danger on the path, I should keep looking in all four directions. After resting, I should turn and look behind me.

academic_translation:
Having examined in front and behind,
I should proceed or else return;
Likewise, in all situations,
Having understood what is needed, I should act.
translation: After checking in front and behind me, I should go forward or go back. In the same way, I should always understand what is needed before I act.

academic_translation:
Having set about an action with the thought,
"My body shall remain like this,"
One should then occasionally look,
Asking, "How is this body remaining?"
translation: When I start an action, I should think, 'My body will stay like this.' Then I should check it sometimes. I should ask, 'How is my body staying?'

academic_translation:
So that the mad elephant of the mind,
Once tied to the great pillar of reflecting on the Dharma,
Does not escape,
One should thus examine with all effort.
translation: I must try with all my effort to watch the mad elephant of the mind. I must tie it to the great pillar of thinking about the teachings so it does not escape.

academic_translation:
So that striving in concentration
Is not lost for even a single moment,
One should thus individually examine the mind,
Asking, "Where is this mind of mine engaged?"
translation: I must try hard not to lose my deep focus for even a single moment. To do this, I must carefully check my mind. I should ask, 'What is my mind doing?'

academic_translation:
When involved in dangers, festivities, and the like,
If one is unable, one should act at ease;
For it is taught that at times of generosity,
Ethical discipline is to be treated with equanimity.
translation: When I face danger or go to a festival, I might not be able to do everything perfectly. If so, I should just relax. It is taught that at times of giving, good conduct should be treated with even-mindedness.

academic_translation:
Whatever one has intended and begun to do,
One should not think of anything other than that;
With one's thought directed toward it,
That very thing should be accomplished first.
translation: When I plan to do something and start it, I should not think of anything else. I should keep my thoughts on it. I must finish that very thing first.

academic_translation:
In that way, everything is well done;
Otherwise, neither will be accomplished.
In that way, the secondary affliction
Of lacking introspection will not increase.
translation: If I act this way, everything is done well. Otherwise, neither task will be finished. In this way, the secondary troubling emotion of lacking watchfulness will not grow.

academic_translation:
Various kinds of idle chatter,
And many sorts of wondrous spectacles—
When engaging in all of them,
One should abandon attachment to them.
translation: There are many kinds of silly talk and amazing shows. When I join in these things, I must stop clinging to them.

academic_translation:
If one digs the earth or cuts grass without purpose,
Or draws lines on the ground and so forth,
Having remembered the training of the Sugata,
One should, out of fear, instantly abandon them.
translation: If I dig the earth, cut grass, or draw lines on the ground for no reason, I should remember the training of the Well-Gone One. Out of fear, I should stop right away.

academic_translation:
Whenever one desires to move,
Or even when one desires to speak,
Having first examined one's own mind,
With steadfastness, one should act with propriety.
translation: Whenever I want to move or even speak, I should check my own mind first. Then I should act firmly and do the right thing.

academic_translation:
Whenever one's own mind has attachment,
Or desires anger at that time,
One should not act and should not speak;
One should remain like a log of wood.
translation: Whenever my mind has clinging or wants to feel anger, I should not act or speak. I should stay perfectly still, like a log.

academic_translation:
If there is agitation or mockery,
Or if one possesses pride and arrogance,
And the intention of exposing others' faults,
Or if there is duplicity or a deceptive mind,
translation: I might feel restlessness or mockery. I might have pride and arrogance. I might think about exposing others' faults. I might have sneakiness or a deceiving mind.

academic_translation:
Whenever one is intent on self-praise,
Or the very disparagement of others,
Or becomes abusive and full of regret,
At that time, one should remain like a log of wood.
translation: Sometimes I feel like praising myself or putting others down. I might say mean things and feel full of regret. At those times, I should stay still like a log.

academic_translation:
Desiring gain, honor, or fame,
Or desiring to seek attendants and retinue,
Or if my mind desires to be served,
At that time, I should remain like a log of wood.
translation: If I want gain, honor, or fame, or if I want to seek helpers and followers. If my mind wants to be served, at that time I should stay like a log.
